A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphMERT research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between sections and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original GraphMERT training, biomedical KG extraction, factuality and validity evaluations, medical question-answering results, and ablations, including appendix evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds comparisons with additional KG generators and judges, retraining experiments, validity filtering, and a helper-LLM ablation.

M1.justification: The encoder architecture, leafy-chain representation, H-GAT, and MLM/MNM objectives remain unchanged. v2 adds an optional second training pass using the expanded KG (Section 6.4.4) and syntactic tail-filtering rules for the smaller-helper variant (Appendix I). These extend the pipeline without replacing its central method.

E1.justification: The PubMed diabetes corpus and diabetes-filtered ICD-Bench, MedMCQA, MedQA, and medical MMLU coverage remain unchanged. Section 6.4.4 newly tests the condition where an expert-curated seed KG is unavailable, using an LLM-generated seed instead. This adds an input-knowledge scenario within the existing biomedical domain.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands the quantitative KG-generator comparison beyond Qwen3-32B by adding Grok 4 Fast and Qwen3-14B in Tables 5–7. Qwen3-14B's earlier use as the GraphRAG backbone was a different role. The downstream GraphRAG comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds Gemini judging, 100,000-triple evaluations for each additional generator, factuality evaluation after validity filtering, alternative-seed retraining, and a 9,000-triple smaller-helper evaluation with additional filters. Existing GraphRAG settings remain stable. The added validity judge is inconsistently named Gemini 2.0 Flash in Table 7 and Gemini 2.0 Pro in Section 6.2.2.

E4.justification: Existing threshold, seed-sparsity, architecture, and error analyses are retained. v2 adds analyses of validity filtering, seed provenance and iterative retraining, helper-model size, and four raw-prediction case studies comparing training objectives. These substantially extend investigation of where reliability gains originate and when they weaken.

E5.justification: Both versions report GraphRAG averages over three runs with seeds 1, 2, and 3. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or dispersion estimates. New missing-verdict columns describe judge responses rather than statistical uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for generators, judges, filtering, retraining, and helper size. Table 5 reports Grok 4 Fast factuality of 79.4 versus GraphMERT's 69.8 under Qwen judging, with the ranking reversed under Gemini judging. The post-similarity-filter count changes from 139,565 to 138,201; Table 7 changes validity from 68.8 to 68.7, although Table 16 retains 68.8. Existing GraphRAG scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, H-GAT equations, attention-decay formulation, training losses, FActScore definition, and injection algorithm retain their mathematical content. The illustrative conjunctive query moves from v1 Equation 1 to v2 Appendix A, Equation 12; other equations are relocated or renumbered.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains reliable KG extraction through a compact graphical encoder. v2's abstract adds validity-cleaning and iterative-refinement claims. The introduction and Section 4.5 more explicitly frame applicability around domains lacking large annotated sentence–triple corpora.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of seed-quality versus factuality tradeoffs, helper capacity, and generic tails receiving favorable factuality judgments despite poor ontology validity. It also explicitly acknowledges helper-induced hallucinations and that billion-token scalability remains untested. These additions materially qualify the mechanisms and applicability of the reliability claims.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link and access information for selected benchmark questions. It newly documents Faiss-based entity linking, preprocessing memory and runtime, GPU memory, extraction batch size and runtime, and smaller-helper filtering thresholds. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures; they do not establish changes to the retained training setup.

R1.justification: New Sections 2.1 and 2.6.1 substantially broaden positioning through structured representation learning and KG-enhanced pretraining/fine-tuning, including K-BERT, DRAGON, and QA-GNN. Section 4.5 explains the choice of LLM comparators relative to supervised BERT/T5 approaches. Earlier background discussions and associated citations are also pruned or condensed.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and reorganizes the background, moves extended neurosymbolic discussion and motivational responses into Appendices A–B, and moves H-GAT exposition into the method section. The original appendices are relabeled C–H, and new experimental and explanatory sections alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Principal comparison tables are redesigned with generator groups, model sizes, multiple judges, missing-verdict columns, and new highlighting. v2 adds filtering, retraining, and helper-ablation tables plus four boxed prediction examples. Existing diagrams and plots are largely retained and relocated; Figure 4's caption corrects the no-leaves case.

improvement.justification: v1's full-KG comparison relied on one LLM generator and one judge, while seed provenance and helper capacity remained untested. v2 substantially strengthens the evidence through additional generators and judging, seed experiments, helper analysis, and reproducibility information. The new evidence exposes judge-dependent rankings and factuality–validity tradeoffs rather than uniformly better performance. Unequal samples and extra filtering limit helper-size attribution, and judge-name and score inconsistencies remain, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evaluating the paper's central claims.
